audit.whatIsWrong: 'She activates Starfire Spellblade at level 2 and immediately becomes a ranged harasser'.
audit.why: Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack empower — 'Kayle's next attack smites her target with celestial fire' — it grants no attack range at all. Attack range comes from Divine Ascent, which Riot describes as 'empowered by the heavens as she levels up and spends skill points... progressively gains Attack Speed, Move Speed, Attack Range'. She is melee until that first form-up. Telling a Teemo she is a ranged harasser from level 2 throws away the entire reason this matchup is 55% — a 500-range champion beating a 175-range one for five levels.
audit.corrected: Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack empower, not a range upgrade. Kayle stays melee until Divine Ascent forms up at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Holy Fervor' is used three times as the name of Kayle's passive, plus 'her passive stacks mean she wins raw level-1 auto trades'.
audit.why: Her passive is Divine Ascent and it has no auto-attack stacking mechanic — it upgrades with levels and skill points. So both the name and the mechanic behind the level 1 claim are wrong, and the claim they support (that she beats Teemo's level 1 auto trade) follows from the invented mechanic rather than from anything in her kit.
audit.corrected: Divine Ascent; it progresses on levels and skill points, not on autos, so there is nothing for her to stack at level 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags 'level chart contradicts data: Teemo wins 55.06% but the chart gives Kayle 4/7 stages vs 1'. The layers also disagree — content win = [Kayle, Kayle, Kayle, Kayle, Teemo, Skill, Skill] while full phases sides = [Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Teemo].
audit.why: The content chart is backwards in both directions at once. It hands melee Kayle levels 1 through 5, which is the exact stretch a 500-range Teemo with on-hit poison owns against a 175-range champion with no dash, and then it hands the item stages to Skill, when two items is where Kayle's ranged on-hit scaling genuinely passes Teemo. The full layer has the early phase right and the very late phase too generous.
audit.corrected: Reconciled to [Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Kayle]: Teemo owns pre-6 outright, level 6 is the Divine Judgment coin flip, Nashor's is his item spike, and two items is where she takes over for good.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'her R makes her unkillable on a cooldown shorter than your full rotation', and 'Her R grants two seconds of invulnerability'. Packet also flags no cooldown-sequencing anywhere.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160/120/80 seconds. At rank 1 that is longer than almost anything else in the lane, and it is the opposite of 'shorter than your rotation' — baiting it out buys you nearly three minutes of a Kayle with no escape. The two-second figure is not in Riot's text and I did not substitute another one. The real sequencing lines here are Radiant Blast at 12/11/10/9/8 (her only reach), Celestial Blessing at 15s flat, and your own Blinding Dart at 7s flat, which is up far more often than anything she owns.
audit.corrected: Divine Judgment is 160s at rank 1, 120s at rank 2. Bait it and you own the next two minutes. Radiant Blast is 12s down to 8s; your Q is 7s flat and always the faster clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states what Divine Judgment does to a damage-over-time champion specifically.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kayle makes an ally invulnerable.' Teemo's entire kill pattern is Toxic Shot poison plus mushroom burn ticking over several seconds — the one damage profile that invulnerability blanks completely rather than partially. It is also castable on an ally at 900 range, so it saves a target you have already poisoned. That is why the level 6 row is a coin flip and it is not written down.
audit.corrected: Divine Judgment's invulnerability blanks a DoT completely — your poison and mushroom ticks are simply erased, and she can cast it on a teammate at 900 range to erase theirs too.

audit.why: 'Kayle without her R is a melee champion with no dash, a free target for W kite-poke cycles' is exactly right and is the best line in the file. Left untouched.
Not an item; repo canonical is 'Liandry's Torment'.

edits.after: Kayle is melee at level 1, 175 range against your 500, and Divine Ascent progresses on levels and skill points rather than on autos, so there is nothing for her to stack — walk up and auto her off every last hit.

edits.after: Starfire Spellblade at level 2 is an auto-attack empower, not a range upgrade — she is still melee until Divine Ascent forms up at 6, so keep poking from outside her 175.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 she stacks Holy Fervor with safe CS and her base stats outvalue yours in the direct early trade before Toxic Shot DoT pressure compounds — she owns the pre-poke phase.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours outright: Divine Ascent gives her nothing to stack off autos, and a 175-range melee Kayle cannot contest a 500-range Toxic Shot auto without conceding CS.

edits.before: Radiant Blast slow and Starfire Spellblade damage let her contest your W kite cycle at levels 4-5 before your Q is maxed; she can stack through your poison and zone back.
edits.after: Radiant Blast is her only reach at 900 and it is 12s at rank 1 — dodge it and levels 4-5 stay a free poke window, because Blinding Dart is 7s flat and up far more often.

edits.before: Kayle pre-6 is a melee champion with no dash and weak base damage — this is your punishment window, but she owns the very early levels because Guerrilla Warfare's camouflage and your W are not yet meaningful against an opponent who simply stands back and last-hits. Her early fragility is real but so is her waveclear; use Toxic Shot poke to zone her off CS and force her to auto through your blind. Do not overextend: she has no gap-close but she can proc Holy Fervor stacks passively and threaten back with Radiant Blast slow. Respect her level-2 power spike where Starfire Spellblade activates, but a Blinding Shot on her melee form completely negates one full auto-attack window.
edits.after: Kayle pre-6 is a melee champion with no dash and weak base damage, and this is your punishment window from the first wave — 175 attack range against your 500, with nothing in Divine Ascent that stacks off autos to change it. Her waveclear is real, so use Toxic Shot poke to zone her off CS and make every last hit cost health. Do not overextend into her jungler, but do not respect her either: Radiant Blast is her only reach at 900 and it is 12 seconds at rank 1, so a dodged Q is a long free window. Blinding Dart on her melee form deletes a whole auto-attack cycle and it is up again in 7 seconds flat, faster than anything she owns.

edits.before: With Liandry's burning her scaling HP and your shroom field denying the side-lane, you remain a genuine threat into the mid-game — but Kayle at two items out-DPS your DoT in a direct duel, and her R makes her unkillable on a cooldown shorter than your full rotation. Shift to shroom-walled splitpush: force her to match you alone, then W-disengage or invisible-reposition off a mushroom the moment she uses R. Never fight her in a skirmish where teammates can hold her R for her; your value is the shroom vision web and a side-lane she cannot contest alone without dying to a stacked mushroom path.
edits.after: With Liandry's burning her scaling HP and your shroom field denying the side-lane, you remain a genuine threat into the mid-game — but Kayle at two items out-DPSes your DoT in a direct duel, and Divine Judgment blanks a damage-over-time kill outright rather than merely reducing it. It is 160 seconds at rank 1 and 120 at rank 2 though, so a baited R buys you a very long window. notes: Two things here are worth a wider look. First, the content chart handed melee Kayle levels 1-5 while the full layer handed the same levels to Teemo — the two layers were exact opposites, and only the full layer was defensible. Second, 'Holy Fervor' is a retired Kayle name that the packet's suspect-name checker did not flag, which suggests the checker only catches near-misses of current names and is blind to names that were correct in an older patch. Same class of miss as 'Grandmaster's Might' in the Jax file.
